light: This is one ordinary frame pulled from a normal handheld video shot by a ranch hand with a consumer camera at eye level, simply recording what happens, not composing a photo. The framing is casual and a little off: something is cut by the edge of the frame. Almost everything in the frame is in focus, nothing blurred out: the kitchen behind stays fully readable. The only light is what the place really has, and each person and object gets light according to where it stands; correctly exposed, daylight from the window and the open door, no lamps. Colours of an ordinary video with automatic white balance and almost no correction: moderate contrast, soft highlights, mild sensor noise and light compression, faint motion blur on anything moving. Skin with pores and uneven tone; hair with stray curls; the denim shirt faded and creased, the leather apron scuffed. Food looks like real home cooking, not styled. People are caught mid-action, unposed.
look: Ordinary handheld video filmed by a ranch hand with a consumer camera at eye level, small natural shakes and casual slightly imperfect framing, everything in the kitchen in focus, only the light the place really has, correctly exposed, automatic white balance, mild sensor noise; real skin and rough working hands; he moves naturally and unposed, nothing staged; no music.

anchors.prompt: Claudio, a weathered 58-year-old Mexican-American ranch cook with curly black hair streaked with gray under a worn natural straw cowboy hat, a short gray-black beard and mustache, brown eyes, sun-tanned lined skin, wearing a faded blue denim work shirt with pearl snap buttons and the sleeves rolled to the forearms, a red bandana knotted at the neck and a worn brown leather apron stands at the black range; a heavy black cast-iron Dutch oven with a heavy black lid that has a visible dent in it on the burner, the water inside boiling hard with big bubbles, steam rising, an old wind-up kitchen timer on the stove beside it. The place: the old cook house kitchen of a working cattle ranch: whitewashed adobe walls, heavy dark wooden ceiling beams, worn terracotta tile floor; a big black cast-iron range with a dented steel kettle on the back, the whitewash above the stove darkened with old soot, a row of black cast-iron skillets hanging from iron hooks on the wall beside it, a coffee can of bacon grease next to the burners. Seen from a ranch hand's handheld camera at eye level, a medium shot from the waist up. clips.text: Two minutes. Turn the heat off. Put the lid on. And walk away. One hour. That's the whole trick. Two minutes of hard boiling, then one hour with the lid on and the heat off.
clips.action: Claudio, the man whose face is the third reference image, sets the heavy dented lid on the boiling pot. daylight from the window and the open door, no lamps. He wears the same worn straw cowboy hat, faded blue denim snap shirt with rolled sleeves, red bandana and brown leather apron the whole time, same curly black-and-gray hair and short gray-black beard, same face as the reference.

clips.text: In that hour, the beans soak up hot water a lot faster than they ever would in cold water overnight.
clips.action: Claudio, the man whose face is the third reference image, points at the closed pot and holds up one finger, 'one hour'. daylight from the window and the open door, no lamps. He wears the same worn straw cowboy hat, faded blue denim snap shirt with rolled sleeves, red bandana and brown leather apron the whole time, same curly black-and-gray hair and short gray-black beard, same face as the reference.

clips.text: The skins soften, the beans swell. When you come back, they're right where they'd be after a whole night of soaking. Except you started them at lunch.
